item.title: ReDiC Curriculum Boosts Faithful Super-Resolution for Smart‑Glasses Images
item.description:
ReDiC Curriculum Boosts Faithful Super-Resolution for Smart‑Glasses Images

Smart‑glasses captures often suffer degradations that hide small text and fine details needed by vision‑language models. A new training curriculum, ReDiC, improves super‑resolution (SR) fidelity while keeping the same SR architecture.

🔍 Overview

  • Introduces a high‑resolution (HR)‑referenced semantic evaluation protocol that compares VLM outputs on restored images with those on HR references.
  • Evaluation uncovers two failure modes:
    • Generative SR may synthesize misleading details.
    • Restoration‑oriented SR may leave critical evidence blurred or ambiguous.
  • These findings drive the need for more faithful detail recovery.

📉 Problem

  • Degradations in smart‑glasses images obscure small text and fine‑grained structures required for visual assistance.
  • Training must present inputs that are challenging yet still recoverable.

🛠️ Method

  • Proposes ReDiC (Recoverability‑Difficulty Curriculum).
  • Combines a model‑independent recoverability proxy with a model‑relative restoration difficulty metric to adapt degradation severity during training.
  • Adjusts severity:
    • Increase when inputs are recoverable and restoration is easy.
    • Maintain challenging but recoverable conditions.
    • Decrease when estimated recoverability is low.
  • Changes only the training degradation generation; the SR architecture and reconstruction objective stay unchanged.

📊 Results

  • Improves average PSNR by ~2.5 dB.
  • Boosts HR‑referenced semantic scores by ~3 points.
  • Gains observed across NAFNet, SwinIR, and MambaIR.
  • Confirmed on synthetic benchmarks, LLM‑based evaluations, and human evaluations.
  • Evaluations performed on 200 real smart‑glasses captures.

💡 Why it matters

  • Enhances the reliability of visual assistance systems that rely on VLMs.
  • Provides a curriculum that keeps SR training both challenging and recoverable, leading to more trustworthy restored images.

#SuperResolution #SmartGlasses #ComputerVision #CurriculumLearning

Source: Learning What to Degrade: A Recoverability-Aware Curriculum for Reliable Smart-Glasses Super-Resolution

item.title: Self-Evolving Curriculum Boosts RL Fine‑Tuning of Large Language Models
item.description:
Self-Evolving Curriculum Boosts RL Fine‑Tuning of Large Language Models

Reinforcement learning (RL) has proven effective for fine‑tuning large language models (LLMs), significantly enhancing their reasoning abilities in domains such as mathematics and code generation. A new automatic method called Self‑Evolving Curriculum (SEC) improves this process by learning a curriculum policy alongside the RL fine‑tuning itself.

🔍 Overview

  • RL fine‑tuning success depends heavily on the training curriculum, i.e., the order in which problems are presented.
  • Random curricula are common baselines but are suboptimal.
  • Manually designed curricula rely on heuristics, and online filtering methods can be computationally prohibitive.
  • SEC is introduced to overcome these limitations.

🧩 How it works

  • SEC treats curriculum selection as a non‑stationary Multi‑Armed Bandit problem, with each problem category (such as difficulty level or type) representing an arm.
  • It uses the absolute advantage from policy gradient methods as a proxy for immediate learning gain.
  • At each training step, the curriculum policy selects categories that maximize this reward signal.
  • The policy is updated using the TD(0) method.

⚙️ Key results

  • Experiments were run in three reasoning domains: planning, inductive reasoning, and mathematics.
  • SEC significantly improves models’ reasoning capabilities, leading to better generalization on harder, out‑of‑distribution test problems.
  • When fine‑tuning on multiple reasoning domains simultaneously, SEC achieves better skill balance.

💡 Why it matters

  • The findings highlight SEC as a promising strategy for RL fine‑tuning of LLMs, addressing curriculum design challenges while boosting performance across diverse reasoning tasks.

#RL #CurriculumLearning #LLM #MachineLearning

Source: Self-Evolving Curriculum for LLM Reasoning - Microsoft Research
